stem: Which of the following factors most significantly increases the likelihood that a pediatric fracture will successfully remodel?

options.text: The fracture is located within the diaphysis of the bone.
The deformity is at a right angle to the plane of motion of the adjacent joint.
There is more than two years of skeletal growth remaining.
The fracture involves significant rotational displacement.

explanation: Significant residual growth, typically more than two years, is a primary requirement for the bone to change shape and accommodate initial deformity.
rationale: Consider the relationship between the time left for growth and the bone's capacity to reshape itself.

optionExplanations.A: Remodeling is generally more effective in the metaphysis than in the mid-shaft or diaphysis of the bone.
optionExplanations.B: Deformities occurring perpendicular to the joint's plane of motion, such as varus or valgus at the knee, do not remodel well.
optionExplanations.C: Significant residual growth, typically more than two years, is a primary requirement for the bone to change shape and accommodate initial deformity.
optionExplanations.D: Rotational deformities are poorly corrected by the natural remodeling process in children.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: There is more than two years of skeletal growth remaining.
